## Chef's Note

Check the rice product before starting: whole wild rice, processed grain and rice blends do not share an identical cooking window. The saved soup lists wild rice. Make the full butter-and-flour sauce separately near the end, then stir in the milk and half-and-half without simmering dairy for the whole slow-cooker cycle.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Start with fully thawed chicken kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual 6-quart cooker’s fill instructions, allowing room for later mushrooms and dairy. Check that the dry rice is suitable for this long-cooking route; instant rice or a blend cannot simply inherit its 6–8 hour clock. Season the chicken with part of the salt/pepper allowance and put it in the cooker.

2. **Start the soup:** Add all the measured stock, dry wild rice, garlic, onion, carrots, celery, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves. Add seasoning as wanted from the unmeasured allowance, cover and start promptly on LOW. Plan 6–8 hours, checking actual rice tenderness and vegetables as well as chicken; processed rice may finish sooner than unprocessed grain.

3. **Add mushrooms and check doneness:** Add all the sliced mushrooms for roughly the final 30 minutes, covering again. The rice and vegetables must be tender, the mushrooms cooked and the thickest chicken pieces must reach 165°F /74°C before removal and shredding. Continue if any endpoint is unmet; do not infer safe chicken from tender rice.

4. **Shred:** Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean board and shred with two forks. Remove and discard both bay leaves from the soup.

5. **Make the sauce:** Melt all the measured butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in all the flour and cook until lightly golden, about 1 minute. Gradually whisk in all the measured milk and half-and-half; cook while whisking until slightly thickened, about 4–5 minutes after adding them, allowing longer if the mixture has not heated and thickened. Season from the salt/pepper allowance to taste.

6. **Combine and serve:** Stir all the chicken and hot milk mixture into the cooker. If too thick, add a little additional half-and-half from its separate allowance. Stir until the soup is hot throughout; cold added dairy can require more heating. Taste before adding more seasoning and serve with the measured parsley if wanted.

## Cooking Notes

Check the actual cooker’s instructions for its permitted food load, liquid requirements and meat size. A common Crock-Pot manual specifies half to three-quarters full, check your model’s own limits. When scaling, choose suitable cooker capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, and divide all measured ingredients across them. Cooking times do not multiply with portions. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions and doneness checks; cook on LOW or HIGH, not WARM.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven to 165°F / 74°C; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

findings.before:
## Chef's Note

A separate butter-and-flour sauce thickens this mushroom, chicken and wild-rice soup near the end. Check the rice for tenderness before adding dairy; processed wild rice can cook much faster than unprocessed grain.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Season chicken with salt and pepper, to taste. Place chicken into a 6-qt slow cooker.

2. **Continue:** Stir in chicken stock, wild rice, garlic, onion, carrots, celery, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves; season with salt and pepper, to taste. Cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours. Add mushrooms during the last 30 minutes of cooking time. Start with fully thawed chicken and check the thickest pieces for 165°F / 74°C before removing and shredding.

3. **Continue:** Remove chicken from the slow cooker and shred, using two forks.

4. **Continue:** Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour until lightly browned, about 1 minute. Whisk in milk and half and half, and cook, whisking constantly, until slightly thickened, about 4-5 minutes; season with salt and pepper, to taste.

5. **Continue:** Stir chicken and milk mixture into the slow cooker. If the soup is too thick, add more half and half as needed until desired consistency is reached.

6. **Finish:** Serve immediately, garnished with parsley, if desired. Discard bay leaves before serving.

A separate butter-and-flour sauce thickens this mushroom, chicken and wild-rice soup near the end. Check the rice for tenderness before adding dairy; processed wild rice can cook much faster than unprocessed grain.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Season chicken with salt and pepper, to taste. Place chicken into a 6-qt slow cooker.

2. **Continue:** Stir in chicken stock, wild rice, garlic, onion, carrots, celery, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves; season with salt and pepper, to taste. Cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours. Add mushrooms during the last 30 minutes of cooking time. Start with fully thawed chicken and check the thickest pieces for 165°F / 74°C before removing and shredding.

3. **Continue:** Remove chicken from the slow cooker and shred, using two forks.

4. **Continue:** Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour until lightly browned, about 1 minute. Whisk in milk and half and half, and cook, whisking constantly, until slightly thickened, about 4-5 minutes; season with salt and pepper, to taste.

5. **Continue:** Stir chicken and milk mixture into the slow cooker. If the soup is too thick, add more half and half as needed until desired consistency is reached.

6. **Finish:** Serve immediately, garnished with parsley, if desired. Discard bay leaves before serving.

## Chef's Note

Check the rice product before starting: whole wild rice, processed grain and rice blends do not share an identical cooking window. Use the dry wild rice listed here. Make the full butter-and-flour sauce separately near the end, then stir in the milk and half-and-half without simmering dairy for the whole slow-cooker cycle.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Start with fully thawed chicken kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual 6-quart cooker’s fill instructions, allowing room for later mushrooms and dairy. Check that the dry rice is suitable for this long-cooking route; instant rice or a blend cannot simply inherit its 6–8 hour clock. Season the chicken with part of the salt/pepper allowance and put it in the cooker.

2. **Start the soup:** Add all the measured stock, dry wild rice, garlic, onion, carrots, celery, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves. Add seasoning as wanted from the unmeasured allowance, cover and start promptly on LOW. Plan 6–8 hours, checking actual rice tenderness and vegetables as well as chicken; processed rice may finish sooner than unprocessed grain.

3. **Add mushrooms and check doneness:** Add all the sliced mushrooms for roughly the final 30 minutes, covering again. The rice and vegetables must be tender, the mushrooms cooked and the thickest chicken pieces must reach 165°F /74°C before removal and shredding. Continue if any endpoint is unmet; do not infer safe chicken from tender rice.

4. **Shred:** Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean board and shred with two forks. Remove and discard all the bay leaves from the soup.

5. **Make the sauce:** Melt all the measured butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in all the flour and cook until lightly golden, about 1 minute. Gradually whisk in all the measured milk and half-and-half; cook while whisking until slightly thickened, about 4–5 minutes after adding them, allowing longer if the mixture has not heated and thickened. Season from the salt/pepper allowance to taste.

6. **Combine and serve:** Stir all the chicken and hot milk mixture into the cooker. If too thick, add a little additional half-and-half from its separate allowance. Stir until the soup is hot throughout; cold added dairy can require more heating. Taste before adding more seasoning and serve with the measured parsley if wanted.

## Cooking Notes

Check the actual cooker’s instructions for its permitted food load, liquid requirements and meat size. Follow your cooker’s stated minimum and maximum fill limits. When scaling, choose suitable cooker capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, and divide all measured ingredients across them. Cooking times do not multiply with portions. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions and doneness checks. Use LOW for this recipe’s cooking route; WARM does not replace cooking.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven outside the slow cooker, stirring or turning as appropriate for even heating and checking 165°F / 74°C throughout; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. USDA additionally recommends bringing reheated soup to a rolling boil; stir and keep the boil brief, since prolonged boiling can change the dairy texture. For hot holding, hold hot food at least 140°F / 60°C in the cooker and follow its holding instructions.
